Simulate marker genotypes from a run's genealogy

Source: R/genotypes.R
simulate_genotypes.Rd

Biallelic genotypes at chosen loci for chosen genomes, painted on the genealogy the run recorded. The model carries no mutation, so a run's genomes differ only by descent: at every position each genome descends from exactly one root genome, a day-1 founder template or an imported genome, and root genomes are unrelated. Each root genome draws its allele at each locus independently, ALT with probability plaf, and every genome carries the allele of the root genome it descends from there. roots records that root genome for every genome and locus, the truth behind the calls: two genomes share a root genome at a locus exactly where ibd_segments() finds them sharing a common ancestor.

Usage

simulate_genotypes(
  run,
  ids,
  loci,
  sample_id = NULL,
  error = 0,
  missing = 0,
  seed = NULL
)

# S3 method for class 'vivax_genotypes'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

run

a run: a vivax_run (from run_sim() or load_run()) or the path of a run directory.

ids

the pedigree ids of the genomes to genotype.

loci

a data frame, one row per biallelic locus: chrom (the PvP01 chromosome, as a number or a name such as PvP01_03_v2), pos (1-based, within the chromosome as this run simulated it) and plaf (the frequency of the ALT allele among the root genomes); optionally locus (an id, by default "<chrom>:<pos>"), and ref and alt for write_vcf(). Other columns are kept.

sample_id

NULL for clone samples, one per genome, or a vector as long as ids grouping the genomes into host samples; a genome can be in several samples.

error

the probability that a call is wrong: a clone call flips, and a host call becomes one of the other two at random.

missing

the probability that a call is missing, after the errors.

seed

NULL, or a whole number that seeds this call alone.

x

a vivax_genotypes object.

...

ignored.

Value

a vivax_genotypes object, a list of:

  • calls: a sample x locus matrix of 0, 1, 0.5 (host samples only) and NA;

  • true_calls: the calls before error and missingness;

  • alleles: an integer genome x locus matrix of 0 (REF) and 1 (ALT), by pedigree id;

  • roots: an integer genome x locus matrix, the pedigree id of the root genome behind each allele;

  • samples (sample_id, n_clones) and clones (sample_id, pedigree_id, in input order);

  • loci: locus, chrom, pos, position (0-based bp along the concatenated genome, as in the IBD segments), plaf, then the other columns given;

  • root_genomes (root_id, tick: day 1 for a founder template, the arrival day for an import, and imported) and root_alleles, their alleles;

  • chromosomes, the run's chrom_map(); type ("clone" or "host"), error, missing, seed (NA when not set) and run.

Details

Each genome can be its own sample (a clone), or the genomes can be grouped into host samples by sample_id, as a blood sample holds every clone in the host: a host call is 0 when every clone carries REF, 1 when every one carries ALT, and 0.5 when both are present.

Reproducibility

The root genomes' alleles are drawn first, for every root genome of the run and every locus, so with one seed, run and loci a genome's alleles do not depend on which other genomes are asked for, how they are grouped, or the error and missingness rates; then the errors, then the missing calls. Large sets of genomes can therefore be genotyped in batches with one seed, and several error rates laid over one truth. A number in seed seeds this call alone and leaves the session's random stream as it was; NULL draws from the session's stream.

What painting leaves out

Root genomes are unrelated, so there is no background relatedness or linkage disequilibrium among them; imports draw from the same frequencies as the founders; an allele never changes along the genealogy; a host sample records which alleles are present, not their proportions; loci are biallelic; and plaf is the frequency among the root genomes, which drifts among the genomes sampled later.

Which genomes can be genotyped

Any genome in the tree sequence: case clones, hypnozoite batches and mosquito products alike. A run with RETAIN_FULL_HISTORY = FALSE keeps few genomes beyond those alive at its end; a run that never started holds none.

Python

The IBD and ARG functions read a run's tree sequence with Python's tskit, through the reticulate package. Either of two routes works. Automatic: with no Python chosen, reticulate sets up its own environment with tskit (>= 1.0) and numpy the first time one of these functions runs; this needs internet once. Your own Python: set RETICULATE_PYTHON to a Python that has those modules (in ~/.Renviron to keep it) before the first such call of a session. A function that cannot reach them stops with an error of class malariafwd_no_python that says what to do, and check_setup() reports what is found.

See also

write_vcf(), ibd_segments(), ibd_pairs(), chrom_map(), episodes()

Examples

run <- example_run()
cm <- chrom_map(run)
loci <- data.frame(chrom = rep(cm$chrom, each = 5), pos = 1000 * rep(1:5, nrow(cm)), plaf = 0.3)
g <- simulate_genotypes(run, classify_cases(run)$pedigree_id[1:20], loci, error = 0.01,
                        missing = 0.05, seed = 1)
g
#> <vivax_genotypes> 20 clone samples x 70 loci on 14 chromosomes
#>   painted on 33 root genomes (23 imported); error 0.01, missing 0.05, seed 1
#>   run: /tmp/RtmpUQ7ECQ/malariafwd-example-run-60b2e786
g$calls[1:4, 1:5]   # what a method sees
#>     1:1000 1:2000 1:3000 1:4000 1:5000
#> 51       0      1      0      0      0
#> 82       0      0      1      0      0
#> 98       0      0      0      1      0
#> 121      0      1      0      0     NA
g$roots[1:4, 1:5]   # the truth behind it
#>     1:1000 1:2000 1:3000 1:4000 1:5000
#> 51       7      7      7      7      7
#> 82      82     82     82     82     82
#> 98       4      4      4      4      4
#> 121      7      7      7      7      7
